subject: Transient egress stewardship & delegation checklist for incident remediation
messages:
From: Dana Park <dpo@medicore.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Transient egress during incident remediation — need commitments

Hi Soojin,

We need to understand Redwood's commitments for temporary cross-region processing in the event of incident remediation or failover. Specifically:
- Maximum duration of transient egress per incident
- Subprocessor roster for EU->US hops and controls on data access
- Audit evidence (S3 logs/KMS proof) you can provide
- Exact language you can accept in a DPA addendum re: stewardship and notification timelines

We're preparing a legal & security checklist; can you confirm whether a 72-hour transient egress window with notification and escrowed keys would be acceptable? Also please attach your current subprocessor roster and a proposed runbook.

Thanks,
Dana Park
DPO | Medicore Health
(attachment: none)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <dpo@medicore.com>, Miguel Santos <miguel.s@medicore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient egress during incident remediation — need commitments

Hi Dana / Miguel — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary of where Redwood stands and a proposed path forward: 

1) Maximum transient egress window
- We can commit to an operational default of 48 hours for transient cross-region processing for incident remediation. 
- Exceptional incidents can extend to 72 hours provided: (a) customer notification within 1 hour of hop, (b) reasoned incident report, and (c) documented approval path from our SRE on-call.

2) Subprocessors and controls
- Attached: subprocessor_roster_2026.csv (current roster with roles and region).
- Access model: only named infra subprocessors (listed) have ephemeral access keys scoped to the incident; access is timeboxed and audited. We can provide a short statement for the DPA addendum that enumerates these constraints.

3) Audit evidence
- We can supply delivery of the following within 5 business days of request: S3 access logs (time-limited), KMS key usage logs, and an ops timeline extracted from our incident tracing system.

4) DPA addendum language
- Attached: Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf — draft addendum with proposed stewardship/notification clauses. Marissa has provided initial redline comments below.

5) Operational runbook
- Attached: runbook-egress-playbook.md (ops-level playbook we will use for transient hops; includes steps, contacts, and proof artifacts).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
- Today: review attachments and flag any unacceptable clauses
- +2 business days: Marissa and Medicore legal sync to agree redlines
- +4 business days: finalize DPA addendum and sign
- +7 business days: tabletop runbook walk-through with your security & our SREs

If that timeline looks tight, we can stretch to two weeks for a full legal review. Would you be able to confirm whether Medicore is OK with the 48h default / 72h exceptional window? Also proposing a quick 30-minute ops call on Friday 9/24 13:00 GMT — I’ll include a calendar invite if that works.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf; subprocessor_roster_2026.csv; runbook-egress-playbook.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <dpo@medicore.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient egress during incident remediation — need commitments

Hi all — I reviewed the draft addendum. High level comments for Medicore legal: 
- Replace any absolute "72-hour" language with "up to 72 hours under documented incident extension with customer notification and approval path." This keeps ops flexibility but gives the customer a clear gate.
- For escrowed keys: we can agree to escrowed KMS envelope keys held in a customer-controlled HSM where feasible; the addendum should allow for "Redwood-assisted rotation and proof" rather than Redwood sole custody.
- Subprocessor roster: we will provide the CSV as an appendix and commit to 30 days' notice for additions that materially change access patterns. Routine infra swaps (non-sensitive) will be covered under the roster and general notice.
- Evidence delivery SLA: 5 business days is acceptable for log exports; if Medicore requires faster access during live incidents we can include a 24-hour expedited path for critical evidence (at cost if outside contractual support hours).

I'll mark up Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf and return with inline redlines by EOD. Please confirm whether Medicore wants the 48/72 approach encoded verbatim or prefers the gate-style formulation above.

Thanks — Marissa
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
(attachment: Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf - redline coming)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <dpo@medicore.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient egress during incident remediation — need commitments

Dana / team — ops confirmation and small ops-level clarification: 

- Runbook: the attached runbook-egress-playbook.md contains our step-by-step for triggering a transient hop, the exact telemetry we capture, and verification artifacts. We enforce timeboxed ephemeral keys and auto-revoke after the declared window; revocation events are recorded in KMS logs.
- 48-hour default is operationally straightforward; to implement the exceptional 72-hour window we require: 
  * customer acknowledgement via the DPA addendum OR a delegated approver email chain (we can accept a named Medicore approver list), and
  * SRE on-call sign-off (we'll capture sign-off in the incident timeline).
- Contacts for a tabletop: me (karthik_iyer@redwood.com), ops cell +1-415-555-0193 (Ops duty), and the SRE rotation list included in the runbook.

I’ll join the 9/24 call (calendar invite to follow). We can demo a sanitized run of the audit artifacts in the tabletop.

—Karthik
Head of Production Reliability | Redwood Inference
Attachments: runbook-egress-playbook.md
